text: The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, who died when they drew near before the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses: Tell your brother Aaron that he must not come whenever he pleases into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain, before the atonement cover that is on the ark, or he will die; for I appear in the cloud above the atonement cover.
This is how Aaron is to enter the Most Holy Place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

versions.text: This is how Aaron is to enter the sanctuary: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
versions.explanation: The same Hebrew term הַקֹּדֶשׁ is rendered 'Most Holy Place' in verses 2, 17, 20, 23 and 27 but 'sanctuary' here (and in v. 16). Consistent rendering of the key term across the chapter helps listeners follow the ritual, since the inner room is meant throughout.

text: He is to put on the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body; he is to tie the linen sash around him and wrap the linen turban on his head. These are holy garments, so he must bathe his body in water before he puts them on.
From the congregation of the Israelites he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron is to present the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
Then he is to take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Aaron is to cast lots over the two goats—one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.

versions.text: He is to cast lots for the two goats—one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew explicitly names Aaron as the subject here (וְנָתַן אַהֲרֹן). Naming him also helps oral clarity after the sequence of pronouns in verses 6–7. A footnote explaining that 'Azazel' is an obscure term, understood variously as the name of the destination, a designation meaning 'the goat that goes away,' or 'complete removal,' would also help hearers.

versions.text: Aaron is to cast lots for the two goats—one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has Aaron placing the lots 'upon' (עַל) the two goats, i.e. assigning each animal by lot; 'over the two goats' keeps that sense while staying idiomatic for reading aloud. A footnote on 'Azazel' would also help hearers, since the term is obscure and has been understood as a proper name, as a designation meaning 'the goat that goes away,' or as 'complete removal'; no such note is currently attached.

text: Aaron is to bring forward the goat on which the lot for the LORD has fallen and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat on which the lot for Azazel has fallen is to be presented alive before the LORD, so that atonement may be made over it and it may be sent away into the wilderness to Azazel.

versions.text: But the goat on which the lot for Azazel has fallen is to be presented alive before the LORD to make atonement, so that it may be sent away into the wilderness to Azazel.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לְכַפֵּר עָלָיו includes an object ('over/by means of it'); the current wording leaves 'to make atonement' dangling without an object and could be misread as the goat making atonement.

text: Aaron is to present the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household; he is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.
Then he is to take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them behind the curtain.
He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the cloud of incense will cover the atonement cover that is over the covenant law, so that he will not die.

versions.text: He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the cloud of incense will cover the atonement cover that is over the tablets of the covenant, so that he will not die.
versions.explanation: הָעֵדוּת means 'the testimony' (the covenant law deposited in the ark); 'tablets of the covenant' adds a noun not in the text. A more literal rendering, with a footnote noting this refers to the stone tablets in the ark, would be preferable.

text: He is to take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the atonement cover, on the east side; then he is to sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times before the atonement cover.

Then he is to slaughter the goat for the people's sin offering and bring its blood behind the curtain. He is to do with its blood as he did with the bull's blood: sprinkle it on the atonement cover and before it.

In this way he will make atonement for the sanctuary because of the uncleanness of the Israelites and their rebellious acts, whatever their sins have been. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which stands among them in the midst of their uncleanness.

No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place until he comes out, having made atonement for himself, his household, and the whole assembly of Israel.
Then he is to go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.
He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleansing it and consecrating it from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
When he has finished making atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he is to bring forward the live goat.

Aaron is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites, all their rebellious acts, whatever their sins have been. He is to put them on the goat's head and send it away into the wilderness in the care of a man appointed for the task.
The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities to a solitary land; the man is to release it in the wilderness.
Then Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments he put on before entering the Most Holy Place, and leave them there.

He is to bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his own clothes. Then he is to come out and sacrifice his own burnt offering and the burnt offering for the people, making atonement for himself and for the people.
He is to burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
The man who sends the goat away to Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may come into the camp.

versions.text: The man who released the goat to Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may come into the camp.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew participle is timeless and this is standing legislation; the past tense 'released' clashes with the present-tense parallel in verse 28 ('The man who burns them').

text: The bull and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place, are to be carried outside the camp; their hides, their flesh, and their dung are to be burned up.
The man who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may come into the camp.
This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month you are to humble yourselves and do no work at all, whether the native-born or the foreigner residing among you.
For on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you; before the LORD you will be clean from all your sins.
It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must humble yourselves; it is a lasting ordinance.
The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve as priest in his father's place shall make atonement. He shall put on the linen garments, the holy garments,

versions.text: The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve as priest in his father's place is to make the atonement. He is to put on the sacred linen garments
versions.explanation: The Hebrew ends verse 32 with an appositional phrase, 'the linen garments, the holy garments' (בִּגְדֵי הַבָּד בִּגְדֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ). The current 'sacred linen garments' collapses the two phrases, and the sentence-final period breaks the flow into verse 33, which continues the same sentence.

text: and he shall make atonement for the holy sanctuary; he shall make atonement for the tent of meeting and the altar, and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.

versions.text: and make atonement for the Most Holy Place, for the tent of meeting and the altar, and for the priests and all the people of the assembly.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew repeats the verb 'make atonement' three times, marking three distinct spheres; the translation flattens this into one verb with a compound list. Restoring the repetition preserves the rhythm of the original and reads well aloud.

text: This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: atonement is to be made once a year for the Israelites, for all their sins. And Aaron did as the LORD commanded Moses.

versions.text: This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: atonement is to be made once a year for all the sins of the Israelites. And it was done as the LORD commanded Moses.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb וַיַּעַשׂ is active third masculine singular ('and he did'), referring to Aaron (or Moses); the passive 'it was done' obscures the agent. Also 'for all the sins of the Israelites' slightly rearranges the Hebrew 'for the sons of Israel, from all their sins.'
